stem: Which index number method is described as the 'ideal' index because it satisfies both the time reversal test and the factor reversal test?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Laspeyres index uses base-period quantities and satisfies neither the time reversal test nor the factor reversal test individually.
Paasche index uses current-period quantities and also fails both tests individually - it has an upward bias for substitutable goods.

Fisher's ideal index = square root of (Laspeyres x Paasche). Because it is the geometric mean of the two biased indices, the biases cancel and it satisfies both the time reversal and factor reversal tests.
The simple aggregative index merely sums current prices divided by base prices with no quantity weighting and satisfies neither test.

explanation: Fisher's ideal index is the geometric mean of the Laspeyres and Paasche indices: F = sqrt(L x P). Its 'ideal' label comes from satisfying the time reversal test (P01 x P10 = 1) and the factor reversal test (P01 x Q01 = V01), properties that no single base-weighted or current-weighted index alone achieves.

explanation_sections.punchline: Fisher earns the 'ideal' label by being the only standard index that simultaneously passes both the time reversal and factor reversal tests.
explanation_sections.approach: This is a direct recall item. Identify the method: Fisher's ideal index = sqrt(Laspeyres x Paasche). Test property: satisfies both TRT and FRT.
explanation_sections.lesson: Laspeyres and Paasche are biased in opposite directions. Their geometric mean (Fisher) cancels the bias and earns both adequacy badges.
explanation_sections.timing: Under 30 seconds. Eliminate options 1, 2, 4 by noting each fails at least one test. Only Fisher (option 3) passes both.
